section: Make in India, PLI schemes, National Manufacturing Policy; ease of doing business reforms
subsections: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs
Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology

accepted.s: The National Manufacturing Policy was notified in which month and year?
accepted.x: The National Manufacturing Policy was notified in November 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the precise month-year rather than the broader year.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a target of the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011?
o: Raising manufacturing's share of GDP to 30 per cent by 2030
Raising manufacturing's share of GDP to 15 per cent by 2022
Raising manufacturing's share of GDP to 25 per cent within a decade
accepted.x: The policy aimed to raise manufacturing's share of GDP to 25 per cent within a decade.
accepted.tq: Test the exact target figure against nearby altered percentages.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Manufacturing Policy, 2011, envisaged the creation of how many additional jobs within a decade?
accepted.x: The policy envisaged creating 100 million additional jobs by 2022, within a decade.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original employment target from later policy targets.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011:
1. Its proposals were sector-neutral.
2. Its proposals were location-neutral.
3. Its proposals were technology-neutral, with an exception for green technology incentives.
4. It provided for infrastructure development through Public-Private Partnership.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The policy was sector-, location- and technology-neutral, except for incentives for green technology, and envisaged infrastructure through PPP.
accepted.tq: When all four statements describe linked policy features, test the complete combination.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups correctly describes the neutrality principle of the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011?
o: Sector-neutral, location-neutral and technology-neutral, subject to green-technology incentives
Sector-neutral, location-specific and technology-neutral, without exceptions
accepted.x: The policy adopted sector-, location- and technology-neutral proposals, while allowing incentives for green technology.
accepted.tq: Separate the three neutrality dimensions from the stated exception.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes a National Investment and Manufacturing Zone (NIMZ)?
o: A rural credit institution for financing manufacturing units
A large integrated industrial township with zoned land use, clean technology and social infrastructure
A tax-free trading port governed exclusively by the customs authority
A small export-only industrial estate without social infrastructure
accepted.x: NIMZs are conceived as large integrated industrial townships with zoned land use, clean technology and social infrastructure.
accepted.tq: Match the official institutional term with its defining features.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
NIMZs differ from Special Economic Zones primarily with respect to which of the following?
1. Size
2. Infrastructure planning
3. Governance
4. Exit policy
5. Fiscal incentives
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The stated areas of difference between NIMZs and SEZs are size, infrastructure planning, governance, exit policy and fiscal incentives.
accepted.tq: Compare institutions through every row of the comparison rather than one feature.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the National Manufacturing Policy, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It specifically included skilling of rural youth as a measure.
It replaced all industrial training with fiscal incentives.
It restricted skill development to metropolitan areas.
It discouraged skilling initiatives for rural youth.
accepted.x: Skilling of rural youth was specifically included among the policy measures.
accepted.tq: Identify the positive policy objective instead of a reversed negative formulation.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of places in Andhra Pradesh is associated with proposed NIMZs that received in-principle approval?
accepted.x: NIMZs were proposed in Chittoor and Prakasam, where in-principle approval was given.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure place pair and reject geographically plausible substitutes.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The TEFS report relating to the proposed NIMZs in Andhra Pradesh was submitted in the context of which period?
accepted.x: The TEFS report was submitted in the context of the State Economic Survey 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Use the exact survey year associated with the administrative update.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Manufacturing Mission, announced in Budget 2025-26, succeeded which earlier policy framework in the manufacturing context?
accepted.x: The National Manufacturing Mission was identified as the successor to the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011.
accepted.tq: Test the successor relationship rather than the announcement year alone.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the targets associated with the National Manufacturing Mission mentioned for Budget 2025-26?
o: 25 per cent manufacturing share and 100 million jobs by 2022
20 per cent manufacturing share and 50 million jobs by 2030
25 per cent manufacturing share and 143 million jobs by 2035
30 per cent manufacturing share and 143 million jobs by 2040
accepted.x: The successor mission was associated with a 25 per cent manufacturing share and 143 million jobs by 2035.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the successor mission’s figures from the original policy’s figures.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: NIMZ is a manufacturing-zone concept, not a monetary policy corridor. DMIC, CBIC and BMEC are listed as industrial corridors.
accepted.tq: Find the one item that belongs to a different institutional category.
accepted.sec: National Manufacturing Policy 2011 - release, objectives, targets, NIMZs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme was designed primarily to provide incentives on which basis?
o: Incremental sales of goods manufactured in India
accepted.x: PLI provides incentives linked to incremental sales of goods made in India; in electronics, the incentive is stated as 4–6 per cent.
accepted.tq: Apply the scheme’s name to identify the production-and-sales trigger.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the PLI scheme?
o: It covers 5 sectors with an outlay of ₹50,000 crore.
It covers 14 sectors with an outlay of ₹1.97 lakh crore.
It covers 20 sectors with an outlay of ₹2.50 lakh crore.
It covers 10 sectors with an outlay of ₹1.20 lakh crore.
accepted.x: The PLI scheme covers 14 sectors and has an outlay of ₹1.97 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Pair the scheme with both its coverage and total outlay.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following sectors:
1. Large-scale electronics
2. Bulk drugs
3. Medical devices
4. Automobiles and auto components
5. Specialty steel
6. Drones
Which of the above are included among the sectors covered by the PLI scheme?
accepted.x: All six listed sectors are among the sectors covered by the PLI scheme. Other listed sectors include telecom, food products, ACC batteries, solar PV, textiles and white goods.
accepted.tq: Verify each sector against the scheme’s sector list before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a sector included in the PLI scheme as listed?
accepted.x: White goods, solar PV modules and specialty steel are included sectors. Coal mining equipment is not included in the listed PLI sectors.
accepted.tq: Use the complete sector list to eliminate the outside item.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the PLI scheme is correct?
1. It supports sunrise industries.
2. In the electronics sector, incentives are stated at 4–6 per cent of incremental sales.
3. PLI-Auto has an outlay of ₹25,938 crore.
4. PLI-Auto requires at least 50 per cent domestic value addition.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: PLI supports sunrise industries, electronics incentives are 4–6 per cent, PLI-Auto has an outlay of ₹25,938 crore, and it requires at least 50 per cent domestic value addition.
accepted.tq: Combine design features, sector-specific figures and an eligibility condition.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the figures given for results up to September 2025, which one of the following correctly represents the incremental production under the PLI scheme?
accepted.x: Incremental production under PLI was reported at more than ₹18.70 lakh crore up to September 2025. More than ₹2.0 lakh crore refers to investment, while 12.60 lakh refers to jobs.
accepted.tq: Separate the adjacent investment, production and employment figures.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The PLI scheme reportedly generated how many jobs up to September 2025?
accepted.x: The reported employment figure was 12.60 lakh jobs up to September 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the unit and magnitude of the employment figure, not the production figure.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PM E-DRIVE was launched by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
accepted.x: PM E-DRIVE was launched by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘which ministry’ trap to distinguish the administering ministry from related ministries.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PM E-DRIVE was launched on:
accepted.x: PM E-DRIVE was launched on 29 September 2024.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact launch date while rejecting adjacent years.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What is the outlay of the PM E-DRIVE scheme?
accepted.x: PM E-DRIVE has an outlay of ₹10,900 crore. ₹11,500 crore is associated with FAME-II.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the new scheme’s outlay from the predecessor scheme’s outlay.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PM E-DRIVE:
1. It succeeded FAME-II.
2. It subsumed EMPS-2024.
3. It provided the first-ever support for electric trucks and electric ambulances.
4. Support for electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers is available up to 31 March 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. PM E-DRIVE succeeded FAME-II, subsumed EMPS-2024, introduced first-ever support for e-trucks and e-ambulances, and supports e-2W/e-3W up to 31 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Check scheme succession, subsumption, novelty and validity period together.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs regarding electric-vehicle support periods under PM E-DRIVE is correctly matched?
o: Electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers — up to 31 March 2026
Other eligible categories — up to 31 March 2026
Electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers — up to 31 March 2028
accepted.x: Support for electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers is available up to 31 March 2026, while support for other categories extends up to 31 March 2028.
accepted.tq: Separate the two validity dates instead of applying one date to every vehicle category.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: FAME-II, which was succeeded by PM E-DRIVE, had an outlay of ₹11,500 crore and covered which period?
accepted.x: FAME-II had an outlay of ₹11,500 crore and covered the period 2019–24.
accepted.tq: Link the predecessor scheme with both its outlay and period.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their announcement or introduction:
A. Make in India
B. Atmanirbhar Bharat package and PLI
C. Semicon India Programme/India Semiconductor Mission
D. PM E-DRIVE
accepted.x: Make in India was introduced in 2014, Atmanirbhar Bharat and PLI in 2020, the Semicon India Programme/ISM in 2021, and PM E-DRIVE in 2024.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two middle initiatives.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: National Manufacturing Policy — Make in India — PLI schemes — India Semiconductor Mission — National Logistics Policy
Make in India — National Manufacturing Policy — PLI schemes — National Logistics Policy — India Semiconductor Mission
National Manufacturing Policy — PLI schemes — Make in India — India Semiconductor Mission — National Logistics Policy
PLI schemes — National Manufacturing Policy — Make in India — India Semiconductor Mission — National Logistics Policy
accepted.x: The sequence is 2011 National Manufacturing Policy, September 2014 Make in India, 2020 PLI, December 2021 India Semiconductor Mission, and September 2022 National Logistics Policy.
accepted.tq: Use the dated milestones to establish the full sequence rather than relying on programme familiarity.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Make in India initiative was launched in which year?
accepted.x: Make in India was launched in September 2014.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise launch year from the policy chronology.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Atmanirbhar Bharat package referred to in the manufacturing-policy chronology amounted to:
accepted.x: The Atmanirbhar Bharat package was valued at ₹20 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Test the package amount directly against closely spaced alternatives.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Semicon India Programme/ISM — ₹76,000 crore
2. ISM 2.0 — ₹1,27,500 crore
3. Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme — ₹62,500 crore
4. Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme after the increase — ₹40,000 crore
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairings are correct: ISM is ₹76,000 crore, ISM 2.0 is ₹1,27,500 crore, MPMS is ₹62,500 crore, and the raised ECMS outlay is ₹40,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Verify each scheme against its stated outlay before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The India Semiconductor Mission was associated with which year and outlay?
accepted.x: The India Semiconductor Mission was associated with December 2021 and an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Pair the programme with both its year and financial allocation.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Policy on Electronics mentioned in the policy chronology was dated:
accepted.x: The National Policy on Electronics was dated 20 February 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact date from nearby policy years and dates.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme approved for FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31?
o: It replaced PM E-DRIVE and offered a 10 per cent incentive on imports.
It replaced ISM and offered a fixed ₹62,500 crore annual subsidy.
It replaced FAME-II and offered a 4–6 per cent incentive on fuel savings.
It replaced PLI-LSEM and offered a 2.25–5 per cent incentive on eligible sales.
accepted.x: The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme replaces PLI-LSEM and provides a 2.25–5 per cent incentive on eligible sales.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the successor scheme, incentive base and rate from related programmes.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme, which additional incentive is associated with domestic sourcing?
accepted.x: The scheme provides up to an additional 1.5 per cent incentive for domestic sourcing.
accepted.tq: Separate the domestic-sourcing increment from the design and R&D increment.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme, an additional 3 per cent incentive is available for:
o: Design and R&D by Indian brands
accepted.x: An additional 3 per cent incentive is provided for design and R&D undertaken by Indian brands.
accepted.tq: Identify the qualifying activity and beneficiary rather than the general sales incentive.
accepted.sec: Recent manufacturing schemes - PLI, PM E-DRIVE, Atmanirbhar Bharat, chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme outlay was raised from ₹22,919 crore to:
accepted.x: The Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme outlay was raised from ₹22,919 crore to ₹40,000 crore in Budget 2026-27.
accepted.tq: Test the revised figure, not the original allocation or another scheme’s outlay.
